thesis: Micron is printing the greatest memory supercycle in history: FQ3 2026 (ended May 28) revenue $41.5B - more than 4x year-over-year and +74% sequentially - at a record ~85% gross margin, with FQ4 guided to ~$50B revenue and ~$31 adjusted EPS. HBM demand from AI servers far exceeds supply and only three companies make it at scale. The stock trades at just ~8x annualized forward EPS yet is down 22% from its high (-14.9% this week on sector sentiment, not company news): the market is pricing the only question that matters - whether these are peak-cycle earnings about to normalize or a structural re-rating of memory economics.
catalysts: FQ4 2026 results (~September 2026): guidance ~$50B revenue, ~$31 adjusted EPS - 20%+ sequential growth on a record base
HBM supply agreements (incl. reported Anthropic-related demand); HBM sold out with demand far outpacing three-supplier industry capacity
Memory pricing momentum: the current crunch has quadrupled revenue in a year
$50B quarterly revenue milestone confirming the structural (not cyclical) thesis if hit
Any capacity-discipline signals from Samsung/SK hynix extending the price cycle
risk_factors: Memory is cyclical: 85% gross margin is unprecedented for DRAM and mean-reverts when supply catches demand; every prior cycle ended with margin collapse
Peak-multiple trap: ~8x forward EPS looks cheap precisely because the E is at a cycle peak - the classic memory value trap
Supply response underway industry-wide; 2027-2028 capacity additions could crack pricing simultaneously with any AI-capex digestion
July 2 sector-wide selloff on cautious AI-demand commentary shows the multiple compresses on sentiment alone (beta 2.14)
Price data conflicted this week ($912.77 vs $984.75 across sources) - tape is fast and disorderly

fq3_2026_revenue.note: vs 9.3B a year ago, 23.9B prior quarter; record ~85% gross margin
fq3_2026_revenue.source: Micron FQ3 2026 8-K press release (SEC EDGAR) / CNBC 2026-06-24
